newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Volga-Dnepr may curtail some cargo flight.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Volga-Dnepr may curtail some cargo flight.

text.p: Russia's Volga-Dnepr cargo airline may stop carrying small cargo shipments from abroad if Russian customs procedures keep changing, a senior official said on Thursday.
Alexei Isaykin, Volga-Dnepr's chief executive, said that ever-changing Russian customs rules created chaos in the air cargo market.
"We will wait for several months and if the situation does not change, the airline will drop out of this segment of the market," Isaykin told a news conference.
Volga-Dnepr's heavy freighters Antonov An-124s and Ilyushin Il-76s make regular weekly flights to three destinations in China to bring mostly small cargo shipments to Russia.
These shipments, which the airline is considering dropping, made up 29 percent of Volga-Dnepr's overall cargo shipments in 1996, Isaykin said.
He also said that this year the company planned to carry more oil and space equipment inside Russia.
"Our An-124s carry only 10 percent of cargo inside Russia and 90 percent go out of the country," he said, adding that Russia's internal air cargo market has a big potential to expand.
Isaykin said that Volga-Dnepr planned to lease a DC-10 freighter soon, but he did not give details.
Last year, Volga-Dnepr carried 45,000 tonnes of cargo or 13 per cent of Russia's total air cargo turnover, second to Aeroflot, which carried 89,500 tonnes or 26 per cent of total cargo turnover.
